stem: A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. What is the probability that the card is either a heart or a face card? (Face cards are Jacks, Queens, and Kings.)

per_option_rationale.rationale: Adds P(heart) + P(face) without subtracting the overlap: (13+12)/52 = 25/52. This double-counts the 3 face cards that are also hearts.
Counts face cards as 4 only (one per suit, e.g., only Kings) instead of 12 (J+Q+K per suit x 4): (13+4-1)/52 = 16/52.
Hearts = 13. Face cards (J,Q,K of 4 suits) = 12. Overlap (heart face cards: J, Q, K of hearts) = 3. By addition theorem: P(heart or face) = (13+12-3)/52 = 22/52.
Reports only P(heart) = 13/52, ignoring the face card contribution entirely and treating the problem as a single-event question.

explanation: There are 13 hearts in a deck and 12 face cards (J, Q, K in each of 4 suits). Three face cards are also hearts (J, Q, K of hearts), so they are counted in both groups. By the addition theorem: P(heart or face) = P(heart) + P(face) - P(heart and face) = 13/52 + 12/52 - 3/52 = 22/52.

explanation_sections.punchline: Count overlap carefully: 3 heart-face cards are in both groups. Subtract once: (13+12-3)/52 = 22/52.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model: addition theorem for non-mutually-exclusive events. Setup decision: identify the two events (heart, face card) and their intersection (heart AND face card = J, Q, K of hearts = 3 cards). Apply: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) = 13/52 + 12/52 - 3/52 = 22/52.
explanation_sections.lesson: Hearts and face cards are not mutually exclusive; you must subtract the overlap. The most common error is forgetting to subtract the intersection (option 1).
explanation_sections.timing: 40 seconds. Identify groups and overlap quickly: 13 hearts, 12 face cards (3 per suit x 4), 3 are both. Sum and subtract. Trap: option 1 (forgetting overlap).
